title: How to Make Zucchini Fries with a Spiralizer
meta_description: Learn how to make crispy, low-carb zucchini fries with a spiralizer! Get a simple recipe and pro tips for the perfect crunch every single time.
html:
If you are looking for a way to get more greens into your diet without sacrificing that satisfying "fry" experience, you are in the right place. While traditional fries are a potato staple, zucchini offers a lighter, low-carb alternative that absorbs flavors beautifully. The secret to getting that perfect, curly shape is using a Vegetable Spiralizer, which transforms a standard squash into elegant, fry-like ribbons in seconds.

Learning how to make zucchini fries with spiralizer equipment is a game-changer for anyone managing a ketogenic diet or just trying to eat more vegetables. Unlike hand-cutting sticks, the spiralizer creates more surface area, which means more space for breadcrumbs and seasoning to cling to, resulting in a crispier bite.

Choosing Your Spiralizer for Perfect Fries

Not all spiralizers are created equal. Depending on your kitchen space and how often you cook, you will likely choose between a handheld model or a countertop version. Handheld spiralizers are great for quick tasks and take up almost no drawer space, while countertop models offer more stability for those who prep large batches of meal-prep veggies.

For these fries, I recommend using the Vegetable Spiralizer. Whether you prefer the handheld ease or the sturdiness of the countertop option, this tool is designed to handle the density of zucchini and carrots effortlessly. The key is to use the thicker blade setting; if the strands are too thin, they tend to shrink and disappear in the oven. You want a sturdy "curl" that can hold up to the coating.

Preparing Your Zucchini to Prevent Sogginess

The biggest complaint people have when making zucchini fries with spiralizer curls is that they turn out mushy. This happens because zucchini is roughly 95% water. If you don't remove that moisture, the fries will steam instead of crisp.

Start by spiralizing your zucchini into long curls. Once you have your noodles, lay them out on a clean kitchen towel or several sheets of paper towels. Sprinkle a generous pinch of salt over the top and let them sit for about 10 to 15 minutes. You will see beads of water rise to the surface. Gently pat them dry—don't squeeze too hard or you'll break the curls—and they will be ready for the breading station.

The Ultimate Crispy Coating Recipe

To get that golden-brown finish, you need a coating that adheres well. I prefer a combination of Panko breadcrumbs for crunch and Parmesan cheese for a savory, salty kick. Here is the process I use:

  • The Dip: Whisk together one egg and a tablespoon of melted butter or olive oil.
  • The Coating: In a shallow bowl, mix 1/2 cup Panko breadcrumbs, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, and a pinch of smoked paprika.
  • The Method: Dip a small bunch of spiralized zucchini into the egg mixture, then toss in the breadcrumb mix until evenly coated.

Pro tip: Work in small batches. If you coat too many at once, the moisture from the zucchini can make the breadcrumbs clumpy before they even hit the pan.

Baking Your Zucchini Fries with Spiralizer Curls

Avoid the temptation to crowd your baking sheet. If the fries are touching, they will release steam and get soggy. Use a large parchment-lined baking sheet and spread the curls out so there is plenty of air circulation around each piece.

Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). High heat is essential for roasting vegetables quickly before they lose their structure. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, flipping them halfway through if possible. You are looking for a deep golden brown color. If you have an air fryer, you can cook these at 375°F for about 7 to 10 minutes for an even faster, crunchier result.

Serving and Dipping Suggestions

These fries are best served immediately while they are at their peak crispiness. Because they are low-carb, they pair perfectly with high-flavor dips. A spicy Sriracha mayo, a cool garlic aioli, or even a simple side of marinara sauce works beautifully. For a healthier option, try a Greek yogurt-based dill dip to lean into the fresh, summer vibe of the zucchini.

If you find yourself with extra capacity in your Vegetable Spiralizer, don't stop at zucchini. You can use the same breading technique for carrots or parsnips to create a colorful vegetable platter that kids and adults alike will actually enjoy.

FAQ

Can I make these fries in an air fryer?

Yes! Air frying is actually one of the best ways to cook spiralized zucchini. Set your air fryer to 375°F and cook for 7-10 minutes. Just be sure not to overfill the basket so the hot air can reach all sides of the fries.

How do I keep the zucchini from breaking?

Use a sharp Vegetable Spiralizer and avoid over-handling the curls once they are cut. When patting them dry or dipping them in the egg, be gentle. Also, ensure you are using firm, medium-sized zucchini; oversized ones often have more seeds and softer flesh, which can lead to breakage.

Can I freeze these for later?

It is not recommended to freeze them after they are breaded, as they will lose their crunch. However, you can spiralize the zucchini and freeze the raw "noodles" in airtight bags. Just be sure to thaw and thoroughly pat them dry before starting the breading process.
